problem_description: The trading chart is currently displaying only a single candle instead of a full historical candle series. This makes the simulator unrealistic and unusable because users cannot analyze trends, support/resistance zones, momentum, or past price action.

expected_behavior.chart_data: Load and render a large set of historical OHLC candles before showing live candles.
expected_behavior.default_range: When a chart opens, it should automatically display enough historical candles to fill the visible chart area.
expected_behavior.minimum_candles: At least 100-300 historical candles should load initially.
expected_behavior.live_updates: After historical candles are loaded, new candles should continue updating in real time.
expected_behavior.scroll_behavior: Users should be able to scroll backward to view older historical candles.
expected_behavior.zoom_behavior: Zooming in/out should dynamically adjust visible candle density without losing history.

data_fetching: Fetch historical OHLC market data from the API before initializing the chart.
Ensure the API request includes a valid timeframe (1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, etc.).
Verify that the API returns an array of candles instead of a single latest candle.
chart_rendering: Pass the complete historical candle array into the chart component.
Render candles sequentially based on timestamp order.
Ensure candle timestamps are unique and properly formatted.
state_management: Store historical candles separately from live streaming candle updates.
Append new candles to the existing candle array instead of replacing the entire dataset.
fallback_handling: Show a loading state while historical data is being fetched.
Display an error message if candle data fails to load.
Prevent chart initialization with incomplete data.

ui_expectation.before_fix: Chart shows only one candle floating in empty space.
ui_expectation.after_fix: Chart should look like a real trading platform with continuous historical market movement visible immediately on load.

impact: Core simulator functionality is broken because users cannot properly analyze or practice trading without historical price movement.
